question: On 14 October 2026, the Commission put forward a proposal to amend Regulation (EU) 2024/1787, postponing certain obligations regarding the import of fossil fuels, including coal, as well as several emission intensity requirements. At the same time, no corresponding postponement has been proposed in respect of the ventilation limits applicable to active coal mines in the EU. 1.

When preparing the proposal to amend the EU Methane Regulation put forward on 14 October 2026, did the Commission carry out a fresh impact assessment to determine how postponing obligations on importers would affect the competitiveness of coal mined in the EU compared with imported coal? Please provide the findings or explain why no such assessment was conducted.

Has the Commission provided Poland with a written response to its request for a fiveyear postponement of deadlines for the limits under Article 22 of Regulation (EU) 2024/1787? If so, please state the date and provide the document setting out its position.

In light of the earlier impact assessment referred to in its answer to question P000985/20231, among others, will the Commission separately analyse the adjustment costs for mines scheduled for closure and consider amending Article 22 where those costs prove disproportionate?
